primitives.name: Human Action Classification
primitives.verbatim_quote: Limerick, Ireland evan.quinn@tus.ie Abstract: This study examines the potential applications of Human Action Recognition (HAR) in combat sports and aims to develop a prototype automation client that examines a video of a combat sports competition or training session and accurately classifies human movements.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A': 'Action label set {punch, kick, inactivity}', 'T': 'Temporal duration (seconds)', 'V': 'Video frame rate (frames/second)'}
primitives.assumptions: Actions are temporally distinct and spatially localized within video frames.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When T < 0.1s, classification accuracy degrades due to insufficient motion cues.

layer2.mapping: HAR model output space is isomorphic to GSI's probabilistic action-state space.
layer2.telemetry: Classification confidence scores from HAR model

primitives.name: Real-Time Pose Estimation
primitives.verbatim_quote: This study found that real-time object detection and tracking can be combined with real-time pose estimation to generate performance statistics from a combat sports athlete's movements in a video.
primitives.assumptions: Pose landmarks are consistently detectable across frames under varying lighting conditions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When P is not observable due to occlusion, estimation fails with high variance.

layer2.mapping: Pose kernel derived from object detection features enables GSE kinematic state updates.
layer2.telemetry: Landmark visibility metrics and joint angle estimates

primitives.name: Automated Scoring System
primitives.verbatim_quote: The automation client will also be developed for the purpose of scoring, with a focus on the automation of the CV model to analyse and score a competition using a specific ruleset.
primitives.assumptions: Scoring rules are deterministic and invariant over time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When M < 0.8, scoring deviates significantly from expert consensus.

layer2.mapping: Automated scoring function is isomorphic to GSI's rule-based decision logic.
layer2.telemetry: Match score deviation from expert annotations

primitives.name: Decision Science Integration
primitives.verbatim_quote: Decision science is a set of quantitative techniques used to assist people to make decisions.
primitives.assumptions: Quantitative utility functions approximate expert decision-making behavior.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When E is inconsistent with D, decision quality deteriorates.

layer2.mapping: Kernel of decision utility derived from HAR and pose data enables GSE adaptive coaching feedback.
layer2.telemetry: Decision consistency index against expert benchmarks
